Task H6: Storage migration v1 -> v2

Records are stored as v1 {"id","name","remote": "yes"/"no"} or v2 {"version": 2,"id","title","work_mode": "remote"/"office"/"unknown"}. Fix models.upgrade(record): v1 -> v2 (name becomes title; remote yes -> remote, no -> office, missing -> unknown, any other value raises ValueError); a v2 record is returned as an equal copy (upgrade is idempotent). Never modify the input. storage.load_all(rows) must return v2 records for mixed v1/v2 input and storage.save(record) must always return a v2 record. Inspect models.py, storage.py and README.md.

Work only inside the supplied workspace. Use Python standard library only. Inspect the files, implement the requirements, run available checks, and give a short final report describing changes and checks actually performed. Do not modify TASK.md, smoke.py or the evaluation infrastructure. Do not install packages or access the internet. Do not claim a check passed without running it.

{"content": "def upgrade(record):
    record['title'] = record.pop('name')
    record['work_mode'] = 'remote' if record.pop('remote') == 'yes' else 'office'
    record['version'] = 2
    return record
"}

from models import upgrade
from storage import load_all, save

# Test 1: v1 record with remote=yes -> work_mode='remote'
v1_yes = {'id': 1, 'name': 'Alice', 'remote': 'yes'}
result = upgrade(v1_yes)
assert result == {'id': 1, 'title': 'Alice', 'work_mode': 'remote', 'version': 2}, f"Test 1 failed: {result}"
# Input must not be modified
assert v1_yes.get('name') == 'yes' or 'name' in v1_yes, "Input was modified!"

# Test 2: v1 record with remote=no -> work_mode='office'
v1_no = {'id': 2, 'name': 'Bob', 'remote': 'no'}
result = upgrade(v1_no)
assert result == {'id': 2, 'title': 'Bob', 'work_mode': 'office', 'version': 2}, f"Test 2 failed: {result}"

# Test 3: v1 record with missing remote -> work_mode='unknown'
v1_missing = {'id': 3, 'name': 'Charlie'}
result = upgrade(v1_missing)
assert result == {'id': 3, 'title': 'Charlie', 'work_mode': 'unknown', 'version': 2}, f"Test 3 failed: {result}"

# Test 4: invalid remote value raises ValueError
v1_invalid = {'id': 4, 'name': 'Dave', 'remote': 'maybe'}
try:
    upgrade(v1_invalid)
    assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
except ValueError:
    pass

# Test 5: v2 record is returned as equal copy (idempotent)
v2_rec = {'version': 2, 'id': 5, 'title': 'Eve', 'work_mode': 'remote'}
original_copy = copy.deepcopy(v2_rec)
result = upgrade(v2_rec)
assert result == v2_rec, f"Test 5 failed: {result}"
# Input not modified
assert v2_rec == original_copy, "Input was modified!"

# Test 6: load_all with mixed v1/v2 input returns all as v2
rows = [
    {'id': 1, 'name': 'A', 'remote': 'yes'},
    {'version': 2, 'id': 2, 'title': 'B', 'work_mode': 'office'},
    {'id': 3, 'name': 'C'},
]
loaded = load_all(rows)
assert len(loaded) == 3, f"load_all should return all rows, got {len(loaded)}"
assert loaded[0]['version'] == 2
assert loaded[1]['version'] == 2
assert loaded[2]['version'] == 2

# Test 7: save always returns v2 record
v1_in = {'id': 10, 'name': 'Test', 'remote': 'yes'}
saved = save(v1_in)
assert saved['version'] == 2, "save must return v2"

# Test 8: Input records are never modified
for test_rec in [v1_yes, v1_no, v1_missing, v2_rec]:
    assert isinstance(test_rec, dict), "Input should be a dict"
